headline: AI Prompt Library: Ultimate Efficiency Hack
summary: An open-source prompt library lets developers discover, version, and reuse battle-tested LLM prompts via a CLI, bringing software engineering rigor to prompt engineering.

slides.title: Stop Rewriting Prompts From Scratch
slides.subtitle: A shared library eliminates repetitive prompt engineering.
slides.body: Developers waste hours crafting similar prompts for common AI tasks. What if a community-driven library gave you production-ready templates instantly?
slides.deep_dive: Prompt engineering often involves reinventing the wheel for recurring tasks like code generation, summarization, or data extraction. This open-source library collects battle-tested prompts, versioned and categorized, so teams can reuse and adapt them instead of starting from zero.
slides.key_fact: Community prompt libraries turn repetitive prompt writing into a reusable asset.
slides.why_it_matters: Reduces prompt engineering time from hours to minutes for common AI workflows.

slides.title: Curated, Versioned Prompt Templates
slides.subtitle: Search, fork, and adapt prompts for any LLM task.
slides.body: The library hosts categorized prompts with metadata, version history, and usage examples. Integrates via CLI or API into your IDE.
slides.deep_dive: Think of it as npm for prompts. Each prompt is a package with a schema, version, and test cases. You can pull a prompt for 'SQL generation' or 'code review' and customize it without losing the original.
slides.key_fact: Prompts are treated as first-class, versioned artifacts.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables prompt reuse, collaboration, and governance across teams.

slides.title: From Search to Production in Seconds
slides.subtitle: Discover → Adapt → Test → Deploy
slides.body: Search by task, clone the prompt, tweak variables, run against test cases, then push to your LLM pipeline.
slides.deep_dive: The workflow mirrors code development: you browse a registry, pull a prompt template, fill in your context variables, run it against a test suite (if provided), and then deploy the rendered prompt to your LLM call. All steps are automatable via CLI.
slides.key_fact: Prompt lifecycle mirrors software development: version, test, deploy.
slides.why_it_matters: Brings software engineering rigor to prompt engineering.

slides.title: Registry, CLI, and Your LLM Pipeline
slides.subtitle: Decoupled components for flexibility.
slides.body: A central registry stores prompts. CLI fetches and renders them. Your app calls the LLM with the rendered prompt.
slides.deep_dive: The architecture has three main parts: (1) a prompt registry (like a package registry) storing prompt templates with metadata, (2) a CLI tool that fetches, renders, and tests prompts locally, and (3) your application which receives the final prompt string and sends it to any LLM provider. No lock-in.
slides.key_fact: Registry + CLI + Your LLM = zero vendor lock-in.
slides.why_it_matters: Works with any LLM provider and fits into existing CI/CD.

slides.title: Developer Query → Rendered Prompt → LLM Response
slides.subtitle: Input: task + context. Output: ready-to-send prompt.
slides.body: You specify the task and context variables. The tool resolves the template, injects variables, and outputs the final prompt.
slides.deep_dive: The input is a task identifier (e.g., 'generate-unit-tests') and a context object (e.g., code snippet, language). The tool looks up the template, performs variable substitution, runs any pre-flight checks, and returns the complete prompt string. Your code then sends it to the LLM.
slides.key_fact: Template resolution and variable injection happen locally, keeping secrets safe.
slides.why_it_matters: Keeps sensitive context out of the registry; only the template is shared.
slides.input: Task ID + Context Variables (code, language, etc.)
slides.processing: Template lookup → Variable injection → Pre-flight checks
slides.output: Complete prompt string ready for LLM API call

slides.title: Don't Treat Prompts as Static Strings
slides.subtitle: Version, test, and review prompts like code.
slides.body: Common mistake: copying a prompt once and never updating. Instead, pin versions, run tests on updates, and review diffs.
slides.deep_dive: Prompts degrade as models change. The library encourages pinning a prompt version, running the provided test suite when a new version is released, and reviewing the diff. Also, avoid hardcoding secrets in templates; use variable injection at runtime.
slides.key_fact: Prompt drift is real; treat prompts as living artifacts.
slides.why_it_matters: Prevents silent failures when models or requirements evolve.
items: Pin prompt versions in your config
Run test suite on every upgrade

slides.title: Add the Library to Your Workflow Today
slides.subtitle: Install CLI, browse registry, ship better prompts faster.
slides.body: Run the install command, search for your task, and integrate in minutes. Join the community to contribute.
slides.deep_dive: Installation is a single command (e.g., `npm install -g promptlib-cli` or `pip install promptlib`). Then `promptlib search <task>` to find templates. Contribute by submitting PRs to the registry. The project is open source and community-driven.
slides.key_fact: One CLI command unlocks hundreds of production-ready prompts.
slides.why_it_matters: Immediate productivity boost for any team using LLMs.

_story.title: AI Prompt Library: Ultimate Efficiency Hack
_story.hook: Did You Know you're typing the same AI prompts hundreds of times? 🤯
_story.headline: Unified Large Language Model Prompt Repository Protocol
_story.fact_summary: AI users frequently re-enter identical instructions, often hundreds of times, across distinct platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. A breakthrough approach now enables the creation of a centralized, reusable prompt library, drastically reducing repetitive input and optimizing interaction with multiple generative AI models.
